observation.visible_scene: The interior of a brick fireplace, lit by an active fire. Several logs are stacked/crossed at the bottom, their surfaces glowing orange-red, with bright yellow-orange flames rising above them against a dark maroon brick back wall. The whole scene is bathed in warm reddish light cast by the fire.
visible_changes: The flames continuously deform: individual tongues of fire change height, lean, split into separate tips, and recombine from frame to frame; a tall central flame and shorter side flames flicker throughout.

Small bright points (sparks/embers) appear at varying positions above the flame tips in different frames (e.g., near the top center in some frames, off to the sides in others), indicating detached burning bits floating upward.
The arrangement and position of the logs at the base stay essentially fixed across the excerpt; their glow persists without obvious collapse or shift.
The brick wall and side walls remain in the same position and framing in every frame, so the camera appears stationary; all visible motion is confined to the flames and sparks.
Overall fire brightness and flame coverage remain roughly steady, with no clear ramp-up or fade-out within the segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the fire was started and what fuel/wood type is being burned.
The full structure of the fireplace and room beyond the visible brick interior.
Whether the fire continues, dies down, or is tended after this excerpt.
The source of the small sparks (rising embers vs. bright flame tips).
uncertain_details: Whether any very slight camera drift exists is not determinable because the background is fixed; motion is attributed to the fire.
Exact material and condition of the logs (charred vs. fresh) cannot be confirmed from lighting alone.
Individual bright dots are ambiguous between detached embers and momentarily bright flame tips.
